title: Mendaña names the Solomons
description: Álvaro de Mendaña, sailing from Peru in search of the land of Ophir, reaches the group and names it after King Solomon's gold.

title: Mendaña dies at Santa Cruz
description: Mendaña's attempt to found a colony on his second voyage collapses in sickness and quarrels, and the Solomons are left alone by Europe for nearly two centuries.

title: Carteret rediscovers the Solomons
description: Philip Carteret in HMS Swallow, separated from Wallis's expedition, is the first European known to return to the group since Mendaña.

title: Bishop Épalle killed
description: The first Catholic bishop of Melanesia is killed on Santa Isabel days after landing, and the mission withdraws for more than fifty years.

title: British protectorate
description: Britain declares a protectorate over the southern Solomons, moved by the abuses of the labour trade and by French and German expansion nearby.

title: Germany hands over the northern islands
description: Germany cedes its Solomon islands, all but Bougainville, to Britain in exchange for concessions in Samoa, completing the present archipelago.

title: Malaita massacre
description: Kwaio fighters led by Basiana kill district officer William Bell and his tax party; a punitive expedition then hangs several of the killers.

title: Honiara becomes capital
description: The government transfers from ruined wartime Tulagi to the new town beside the Guadalcanal battlefields.

title: Self-government
description: Britain grants internal self-government under chief minister Peter Kenilorea on the way to independence.

title: Independence
description: The Solomon Islands become independent within the Commonwealth after 85 years of British rule.

title: Cyclone Namu
description: The worst cyclone in the country's recorded history kills over a hundred people and wrecks villages on Malaita and Guadalcanal.

title: The Tensions begin
description: Guadalcanal militants begin driving Malaitan settlers from the island, starting five years of ethnic conflict that paralyse the state.

title: Malaita Eagle Force coup
description: The Malaita Eagle Force, with the paramilitary police, seizes Honiara and forces prime minister Bartholomew Ulufa'alu to resign at gunpoint.

title: RAMSI intervention
description: At the government's request an Australian-led Pacific force lands to disarm the militias and rebuild the state, staying fourteen years.

title: Earthquake and tsunami
description: A magnitude-8.1 earthquake off the Western Province sends a tsunami onto Ghizo and its neighbours, killing 52 people and destroying many villages.

title: RAMSI withdraws
description: The Regional Assistance Mission ends after fourteen years, leaving a rebuilt police force and civil service.

title: Switch to China
description: The government ends 36 years of diplomatic ties with Taiwan and recognises the People's Republic of China, over the fierce objection of Malaita's premier.
